title: Dagging ewes before lambing
subtitle: Clearing wool from hindquarters to reduce fly strike risk and ease lambing.
excerpt: Dagging is the removal of soiled or excessive wool from the sheep's hindquarters and around the tail dock. Done in late pregnancy, it reduces fly strike risk in early spring, makes it easier to see when a ewe is close to lambing, and keeps the udder area cleaner for the newborn lamb's first feed.
sourceNotes: NSA (National Sheep Association), pre-lambing management guidance. NADIS, Blowfly Strike (2023). SAC Consulting, sheep management at lambing.

glossaryTerms.definition: The removal of dag (hardened, soiled wool) and excess wool from the breech and around the tail dock of a sheep. Also called crutching in Australia and New Zealand.

A condition in which blowflies (Calliphora, Lucilia species) lay eggs in soiled or moist wool, particularly around the breech. The hatched larvae feed on the sheep's skin, causing rapid tissue damage and death if untreated.

Dag ewes 4 to 6 weeks before the expected lambing date. This allows time to identify and treat any skin irritation found under the dag, and gives the clipped area time to dry and harden before lambing. Dagging immediately before lambing increases the risk of chilling the ewe if the weather turns cold.
All crusted dag around the tail, vulva, and down the inner thighs as far as any soiling reaches.
Clean wool within 5 cm of the vulva and around the udder, to leave a clear, visible area for lambing assessment and for lambs finding the teat.
Any wool wet or stained from scouring, even if there is no dag crust.
Back the ewe into a corner or set her up on her rump for restraint.
Use hand shears or a battery clipper to remove the dag and the surrounding wool. Work from the centre of the tail dock outward toward the inner thighs.
Check the skin under any wet dag for signs of irritation, fly eggs, or larvae. Any evidence of strike should be treated immediately.
Remove the dag from the pen and dispose of it away from the flock. Dag left in the pen is attractive to blowflies.
